elements.content: Grammar focus: Passive: Simple and Future Tenses.

Find the tense the sentence needs, put it on be, and leave the participle alone. Then decide whether the agent earns a by-phrase: it does when the reader needs to know who acted, and it does not when the actor is obvious, unknown or irrelevant.

present simple — is / are + participle: the file is checked daily
past simple — was / were + participle: the contract was signed in June
future — will be + participle: the results will be published
present continuous — is / are being + participle: the office is being repainted
past continuous — was / were being + participle: the room was being cleaned
agent with by — only when it matters: signed by both directors
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'The report ___ every quarter.'
2. Complete: 'The site ___ next month.'
3. Which sentence keeps the topic first?
options: The file was checked by the auditor.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

The file is checked daily. — Present simple passive. (Is + participle.)
The contract was signed in June. — Past simple passive. (Was + participle.)
The results will be published. — Future passive. (Will be + participle.)
What do you observe?

The passive takes the tense on be and leaves the main verb as a past participle. Present simple: is checked. Past simple: was signed. Future: will be published. Present continuous: is being repainted. Past continuous: was being checked. The agent appears in a by-phrase only when it matters: the contract was signed by both directors.
1. Which word carries the tense in a passive?
2. Which form is the future passive?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can describe how the internet shapes behaviour.

Success criteria:
- I can form the present and past simple passive.
- I can form the future passive.
- I can decide when to keep the agent in a by-phrase.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The contract was sign in June (base verb instead of a participle) → ✅ The contract was signed in June
❌ The results will published on Friday (missing be) → ✅ The results will be published on Friday
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

Each invoice is verified against the order.
The minutes were circulated after the meeting.
The panels will be replaced in April.

- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
